source.title: Neurons in a forebrain nucleus required for vocal plasticity rapidly switch between precise firing and variable bursting depending on social context

confidence_rationale: Single-unit LMAN recordings show the diversity signal is a state-gated variable -- the same neurons switch between precise single-spiking (low variability) and variable bursting (high variability) with social context, while the average song-locked signal is preserved. Directly evidences MECH-341's 'signal weight amplified to competitive parity' as a real, rapidly tunable knob. Indirect on the scoring locus; lower mapping fidelity.
failure_signatures: When the diversity channel is in its low-variability (directed-song) state, LMAN fires precise single spikes locked to song and trial-to-trial variability is minimal -- behaviour is near-deterministic. If a REE diversity circuit is left in a low-weight state, the candidate pool will not be carved into distinct classes at selection.

Different LMAN neurons in the same bird show distinct firing patterns, suggesting subsets jointly encode song features -- a single scalar 'exploration temperature' would under-describe the diversity signal, which is distributed and structured.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Individual LMAN neurons reversibly transform their signaling mode with social context: precise, reliable single-spiking locked to song when a male sings to a female ('directed'), versus prominent burst firing and high trial-to-trial variability when singing alone ('undirected'). The average song-locked signal is similar across contexts, indicating a common underlying signal modulated by a state-dependent variability component.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-341 requires not just that a diversity circuit exist but that its signal weight be amplifiable to competitive parity with the deterministic pathway -- i.e. that diversity is a controllable state rather than a fixed property. Kao et al. show the variability output of the basal-ganglia-loop nucleus LMAN is exactly such a rapidly switchable, context-gated state, dissociable from the underlying song-locked signal. This evidences the tunable-weight half of MECH-341: the same circuit can be driven toward exploration (high variability) or exploitation (precise, deterministic) on demand.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is about state-gating of an output-stage variability signal, not about a value-scoring aggregation step preserving candidate diversity; the link to MECH-341's named locus is indirect. The gating variable here is social context (a behavioural state), which has no direct REE analog beyond 'something modulates the diversity weight'. Songbird vocal system -> REE E3/CEM transfer.
mapping.source_context: Adult male zebra finches; single-unit recordings in LMAN during directed vs undirected singing.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality single-unit work in a strong venue. Mapping fidelity is the lowest of the three MECH-341 entries (0.5) because the result is about context-gating of an output variability signal, one step further from the scoring locus than Kojima/Olveczky. Included because it is the cleanest evidence that the diversity 'weight' is a real, rapidly tunable state, which is the specific sub-clause of MECH-341 about amplifying the diversity circuit to parity.
